title: Lok Sabha USQ 2499, 2 Sep 1981 (Kumbha Ram Arya): Declaring Mahajan Field Firing Range, Bikaner a firing and artillery practice range
villages_named: dhannasar? (धनसर, p.177 - said to be OUTSIDE the notified area; identification uncertain)
what_it_contains: Hindi written answer (Shivraj V. Patil). Mahajan range notified under the Manoeuvres, Field Firing and Artillery Practice Act 1938, s.9(1): first in October 1975 for five years (to Sept 1980), extended to May 1981, then by Rajasthan Govt for 1 July 1981 to 30 June 1986. Under s.9(2) actual firing notified Dec 1975-Jun 1976, Dec 1976-Jun 1977, Jul 1977-Jun 1978 (list continues). Accidents: a civilian of village Dhanasar killed by an unexploded 84mm HEAT rocket at home, three sons injured, no compensation because village outside notified area; night of 23-24 Feb 1981 house of a resident of Motlai burnt by pyrotechnic ammunition, Rs 7,560 paid 28 Mar 1981; March 1981 claims via Tehsildar Lunkaransar for two camels (Motlai), two bullocks and four cows (Dhanasar) - Rs 6,000/5,000/10,000 claimed.
why_relevant: Primary evidence of the pre-acquisition legal status (Manoeuvres Act notifications from 1975) and of the notification series; names Motlai and Dhanasar. Names private individuals (victims).

title: Lok Sabha, 14 Sep 1981, Matter under Rule 377 (Daulat Ram Saran, Churu): Firing range required by Ministry of Defence in Bikaner

A committee chaired by Tej Kumar (Rajasthan canal area development) on 28 Nov 1979 found the 34-village area unsuitable, but during Governor's rule the Bikaner Collector recommended it. Suggests alternative barani land in Bikaner/Kolayat tehsils.

what_it_contains: The "Hazari Ram" case. Land acquired for MFFR; rehabilitation Notification No. F.3(8) GSR.162/Reve./Col./81 dated 23-11-1985, published Rajasthan Gazette Extraordinary Part IV-C(1) dated 10-1-1986 at page 339, issued under Rule 24 of Rajasthan Colonization (Allotment and Sale of Govt Land in IGC Colony Area) Rules 1975, Rule 17 of Rajasthan Land Revenue (Allotment of Land for Agricultural Purposes) Rules 1970 and s.264 Rajasthan Land Revenue Act 1965. Hazari Ram allotted 40 bighas, paid Rs 12,000 (14-8-1986) and then Rs 31,500 (15-4-1987). Land of 54 displaced allottees became command in 1987 (Rajmalsar and Jaimalsar minors); circular 19-10-1987 demanding extra price quashed; appeals dismissed.
